raw_response:
Aiya, let me think about this year's planning. I've been doing wheat and maize on this same little piece of ground for more years than I can count, so I mostly just do what I've always done.

---

## My thinking this year

I'm 73 now, and it's just me and my old woman at home. Our children are working in the city, they don't come back for the farming. 3 mu isn't much but at our age it's already plenty — the body isn't what it used to be. We can't do like the young farmers.

**About the wheat** — I already planted it back in October, around the 10th like always. That's when everyone around here puts it in. I used the seed I bought from the供销社 (supply cooperative), same variety my neighbor老李 has been using, yields are stable. Before planting I spread one bag of 复合肥 (compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind) per mu, about 40 jin or so. When the wheat greens up in spring — that should be around 清明 (Qingming, early April) — I'll topdress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu. If it looks yellow and weak I put a little more, if it looks strong I save some money.

For water — this year we already gave it the 冻水 (winter water) before the ground froze. After green-up I'll water it once, then again at 拔节 (jointing), and if May is dry I water it one more time before the grain fills. Four times total usually. The well electricity isn't cheap, but wheat without water on this plain gives you nothing.

**About the maize** — That's the one coming up. As soon as the combine cuts the wheat in early June, I have to get the maize in within a few days, otherwise it's too late. No time to plow properly — I just use 免耕播种 (no-till seeder), hire the machine from村里 (the village), costs about 30 yuan per mu but it does planting and fertilizer together, saves my old back. I'll use Zhengdan or one of the common hybrids, whatever the seed shop has that my neighbors are planting — I don't take chances with new varieties at my age.

At planting I put base fertilizer down with the machine, about one bag of compound per mu. Then when the maize is about knee-high (大喇叭口, big flare-leaf stage around late July), I topdress urea, maybe 20-25 jin per mu. If there's a good rain I don't need to irrigate; if July-August is dry I water once or twice. Maize is tougher than wheat about water.

**Pests and weeds** — I spray herbicide once on the wheat in spring, once on the maize after planting. That's standard. For insects, only if I see aphids bad on the wheat will I spray — otherwise I save the money. My eyes aren't good enough to spot bugs early anyway, so I mostly rely on what other villagers are saying when we talk in the street.

**The money side** — Total I'll probably spend around 1800-2000 yuan on inputs for the whole 3 mu both seasons. We get some subsidy money from the government for grain. At our scale we don't make much, maybe break even after costs, but the grain feeds us and we sell a bit. At 73, I'm not trying to get rich — I just want to keep the land going while I still can.
